study: retrospective real-bug ordering comparison; two patched known bugs

benchmarks.name: BugsInPy historical bug metadata; upstream source cloned only

common_design.risk: Test file postdates bug fix and includes targeted regression test by original maintainers
common_design.python_runner: 3.8.x on Ubuntu 22.04, historical case metadata Python 3.7.0
common_design.method: One unittest execution per source version; statuses reused in policy calculations
common_design.detecting_test: FAIL assertion in buggy and PASS in fixed

conclusion: No policy found either known bug by budget 12; all three strategies failed equally under the preregistered budget. No relative superiority can be inferred. Test composition, access to a useful signal or more budget is a future question, not a demonstrated explanation.
limitations: Only two previously patched faults from two projects; no generalization or independent discovery.
The source test banks are fixed-revision suites, potentially written to reveal the known faults.
Single fixed-seed random permutation is a sampled policy, not a representation of average random performance; exact expectation calculated separately.
The same suite is run once per version and budget scores are derived from those results; no test independence or state-free execution guaranteed.
Historical upstream Python 3.7.0 vs CI Python 3.8.x.
Test method errors are not counted as bug detections; conservative scoring can undercount.
CI jobs passed; this only validates protocol and historical reproduced results, not efficacy of strategies.
